method: You.com livecrawl + Exa against the nine evidence gaps the dossier itself names; Firecrawl capture of every primary artifact returned. 162 results, 114 dated, 7/7 primary captures.

deltas.was: STRADVISION is treated as an independent perception-layer comparator; Aptiv Gen 6 is treated as a whole-stack rival.
deltas.now: Aptiv's Gen 6 smart camera features STRADVISION's AI-based vision technology. The two are not separate rivals — one is embedded inside the other.
deltas.source: Aptiv PLC press release, 6 January 2026, aptiv.com newsroom
deltas.so_what: The thesis is proven by a rival: a Tier-2 perception layer inside an accountable integrator's platform is exactly the position DeepGrid is bidding for, and STRADVISION already holds it in the winning stack. DeepGrid's competition is not Aptiv — it is the incumbent perception layer inside Aptiv.
deltas.rating_move: raise STRADVISION from comparator to occupant of the target position

deltas.was: Structural AEBS strength; programme specifics still need corroboration.
deltas.now: ZF Commercial Vehicle Control Systems India secured an ADAS business nomination from a leading Indian E-Mobility CV OEM: 16 features including AEBS, BSIS, DDAWS, LDWS, MOIS across 13.5m coaches, 55-ton trucks and 7/9/12m buses; validated over 300,000 km on Indian roads; ARAI certified; compliant with GSR 184e.
deltas.source: ZF CVCS India press note, 3 December 2025, zf.com
deltas.so_what: The India CV nomination is no longer an inference. ZF holds a certified, road-validated, regulation-compliant suite with a named OEM category — the control-point argument is now evidenced rather than asserted.
deltas.rating_move: ZF N2/N3 OEM threat: corroborated, hold at HIGH

deltas.was: Credible perception-layer comparator; India CV specifics not established.
deltas.now: A global commercial vehicle OEM selected SVNet for deployment across its India vehicle lineup, targeting fleet-scale ADAS in India's CV segment, on low-cost resource-constrained hardware.
deltas.so_what: The falsifier the dossier set for STRADVISION has fired. 'Global scale is not India CV proof' was the right test, and STRADVISION has now passed it — including on the constrained-compute ground DeepGrid claims as its own differentiator.
deltas.rating_move: STRADVISION India CV: insufficient evidence -> verified fact

deltas.was: ~$2.5m initial revenue across 3,000 heavy trucks; deployment quality unproven.
deltas.now: A further $5.3m agreement to equip 3,600 electric buses and trucks in India, spanning public transport, seaport logistics, mining and industrial transport. Roadzen investor materials confirm the original $2.5m / 3,000-truck award.
deltas.source: Roadzen Inc. via GlobeNewswire, 23 June 2026; Roadzen investor relations, 29 April 2026
deltas.so_what: drivebuddyAI has more than doubled its committed fleet in two months and crossed from trucks into buses and mining — the arena the dossier nominates as DeepGrid's fastest proof route. The fleet-aftermarket window is closing faster than the dossier assumes.
deltas.rating_move: drivebuddyAI fleet threat: raise; mining is now contested

deltas.was: Rebase the regulatory plan to notified 2027-28 dates; correct April-2026 claims.
deltas.now: The operative instrument is GSR 184e, cited by ZF as the regulation its India suite complies with, and by Aptiv as '2027 regulations' for trucks and buses. Draft AIS-162 covers AEBS for M2/M3/N2/N3; AIS 184 is cited in fleet-side announcements.
deltas.source: ZF CVCS India press note (GSR 184e); Aptiv press release (2027); MoRTH draft AIS-162
deltas.so_what: The correction holds and now has a name to cite. Naming GSR 184e in client-facing material is defensible; naming an April-2026 mandate is not. The gazette notification itself remains uncaptured.
deltas.rating_move: regulatory correction: corroborated, gazette still outstanding

deltas.was: No corroborated fact yet proves Gahan leads; independent profiling needed.
deltas.now: Two engines, livecrawl enabled, 18 results: zero primary sources on Gahan Technologies. No company release, no OEM milestone, no qualification artifact.
deltas.source: You.com livecrawl + Exa, 14 August 2026 — measured absence, not an unrun search
deltas.so_what: The gap is now a measured absence rather than an unchecked assumption. Gahan was ranked the highest-priority diligence target on the strength of claims that leave no public trace; that ranking should fall until a primary artifact exists.
deltas.rating_move: Gahan diligence priority: lower, pending any primary artifact

deltas.was: Exchange-filed January 2026 partnership; no named Indian OEM nomination, SOP, deployment or homologation.
deltas.now: Confirmed across four independent outlets on 19 January 2026. MINIEYE is Hong Kong-listed and China-based; Sterling Tools handles application engineering and perception tuning for Indian road conditions. Still no named OEM nomination or SOP.
deltas.source: The Hindu BusinessLine, Business Upturn, Newsfile, Globe and Mail, 19 January 2026
deltas.so_what: The partnership is real and the division of labour is now explicit — which makes it a direct template for DeepGrid's own attach-and-prove move, and a China-sourced perception layer competing for the same slot.
deltas.rating_move: hold; the falsifier (named OEM nomination) still stands unfired

deltas.was: bitsensing $25m Series B attributed; Netrasemi adjacent compute, not a direct ADAS competitor.
deltas.now: bitsensing's $25m Series B is confirmed on its own newsroom, with an NXP radar partnership. Netrasemi's A2000 edge-AI SoC is production-ready with automotive trials under way and a mid-2027 commercial target.
deltas.so_what: Both hold. Netrasemi's mid-2027 target coincides with the GSR 184e window, so 'adjacent' has an expiry date — the coexistence test should be re-run before mid-2027 rather than treated as settled.
deltas.rating_move: hold both; add a dated re-test on Netrasemi
